question: A newsletter editor needs a Claude-drafted piece to quote the organisation's own published figures accurately. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) Ask Claude to draft the piece; gather the published figures; check the draft's numbers against them; send the piece out to readers.
B) Gather the published figures; check the draft's numbers against them; give them to Claude as the material; send the piece out to readers.
C) Gather the published figures; give them to Claude as the material; check the draft's numbers against them; send the piece out to readers.
D) Give them to Claude as the material; send the piece out to readers; gather the published figures; check the draft's numbers against them.
correct_answers: C) Gather the published figures; give them to Claude as the material; check the draft's numbers against them; send the piece out to readers.
explanations: Incorrect. Drafting before the figures are supplied invites Claude to fill the gaps, which creates the errors the later check then has to catch.
Incorrect. The numbers are checked before a draft exists, and the source material reaches Claude only after the piece has been written.
Correct. Supplying the authoritative figures first keeps the draft grounded, and the check afterwards confirms nothing drifted during writing.
Incorrect. The piece goes to readers before the figures have been gathered or any check has taken place.
